$schema-note: Mechanically verified by src/__tests__/workers/worker-policy-manifest.test.ts: completeness (candidate module set, derived from the R42 primitive-anchored grep in the security-review-followups plan C5, vs. manifest `modules`/`entrypoint`/`$documented-exclusions`, both directions), `rawSql` (/\$queryRaw|\$executeRaw/ grep across an entry's modules), `destructive` (/deleteMany|DELETE FROM/i grep), `emitsAudit` (/logAudit|enqueueAudit|AUDIT_ACTION/ grep), `usesSecurityDefiner` (grep of the SECURITY DEFINER function names extracted from prisma/migrations/20260522000200_audit_log_revoke_via_definer/migration.sql: audit_log_purge, audit_log_tenant_migrate), file existence of every `entrypoint`/`modules` path. Doc fields (`tenantScoped` reason, `idempotent`, `retryPolicy`, `poisonMessageHandling`, `retentionPolicyTouched`) are presence + >=10-char-prose verified only; their accuracy is a human review concern (SC3), same trust level as route-policy-manifest.json's `handlerAuthReason`. Per the worker-runtime-invariants plan C5, `sweepBounds` (every `rawSql: true` entry) and `runtimeBounds` (audit-outbox-worker only) are additionally mechanized: every DELETE/UPDATE write statement the shared SQL scanner (scripts/checks/lib/sql-scan.mjs) reads in an entry's modules must be single-row by its table's primary key, capped by a materialized key set (`WITH <cte> AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT <keys> ... LIMIT n) ... WHERE (<keys>) IN (SELECT <keys> FROM <cte>)` as a top-level AND conjunct), or covered by exactly one tight, used `sweepBounds.exemptions[]` entry, and `runtimeBounds` values are cross-checked against the literal constants in src/lib/constants/audit/audit.ts and the `@default(8)` maxAttempts lines in prisma/schema.prisma.

tenantScoped.reason: Every claim/deliver/reap/purge transaction sets bypass_rls + app.tenant_id=NIL_UUID + its grant's tables via setBypassGucs (audit-outbox-worker.ts) and then operates per-row using the row's own tenant_id column (e.g. deliverRow, deliverRowWithChain) -- it is a system-wide sweep by role privilege, but every write is attributed to the row's own tenant.

audit-outbox-worker.idempotent: claimBatch (via claimOutboxBatchInTx) picks at most batchSize PENDING ids in a MATERIALIZED CTE with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and flips only those rows (re-checking status='PENDING'), so concurrent workers claim each row exactly once; deliverRow/deliverRowWithChain INSERT INTO audit_logs ... ON CONFLICT (outbox_id) DO NOTHING so a re-delivered row after a crash is a no-op (audit-outbox-worker.ts claimOutboxBatchInTx, deliverRow, deliverRowWithChain).
audit-outbox-worker.retryPolicy: recordError computes exponential backoff with full jitter (computeBackoffMs + withFullJitter, audit-outbox-worker.ts recordError) and reschedules via next_retry_at; a row exceeding max_attempts transitions to FAILED (dead-letter) instead of retrying forever (audit-outbox-worker.ts recordError, isDead branch).
audit-outbox-worker.poisonMessageHandling: Rows at/over max_attempts are marked FAILED and an AUDIT_OUTBOX_DEAD_LETTER event is written directly to audit_logs (bypassing the outbox, to avoid recursion) in the same transaction via writeDirectAuditLogInTx (audit-outbox-worker.ts recordError, isDead branch); reapStuckRows separately reaps at most REAP_BATCH_SIZE PROCESSING rows stuck past PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_MS per pass, dead-lettering those already at max_attempts (audit-outbox-worker.ts reapStuckRows, reapStuckRowsInTx).

exemptions.reason: Anchor advance is single-row by PK (WHERE tenant_id = $3, tenant_id is audit_chain_anchors' primary key); not a multi-row sweep.

tenantScoped.reason: The NOBYPASSRLS passwd_retention_gc_worker role runs each globalDelete / per-tenant sweep entry in a transaction whose bypass_rls is set by the module-private dispatcher (sweep.ts inSweepTx; each sweep asserts it) to span all tenants under existing RLS policies, but every EXPIRY_AUDIT_PROVENANCE / PER_TENANT_FN / PER_TENANT_TRASH / PER_TENANT_AGE entry enumerates or attributes rows by their own tenant_id (sweep.ts sweepAuditLogs, sweepPerTenantAge, sweepTrashEntry) -- a deliberate all-tenant blast radius (registry.ts, the globalDelete field doc), never a cross-tenant write of one tenant's data into another.

retention-gc-worker.idempotent: Each EXPIRY/EXPIRY_GUARDED/EXPIRY_AUDIT_PROVENANCE DELETE is batch-bounded by a MATERIALIZED key-set CTE (WITH picked AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT keys ... LIMIT $1) DELETE ... WHERE (keys) IN (SELECT keys FROM picked)) keyed off cutoffColumn < now(), so a re-run after a crash simply finds fewer (or zero) newly-expired rows -- no duplicate side effects (sweep.ts sweepExpiryEntry, sweepGuardedExpiryEntry, sweepAuditProvenanceEntry). sweepAuditLogs routes through the audit_log_purge SECURITY DEFINER function which is itself a plain bounded DELETE (registry.ts, the PER_TENANT_FN audit_logs entry; sweep.ts sweepAuditLogs).
retention-gc-worker.retryPolicy: No per-row retry/backoff: sweepOnce catches each registry entry's error individually (INV-C4b), logs {table, code} only, records counts[table]=-1, and continues to the next entry -- the NEXT scheduled sweep tick (fixed intervalMs, no backoff) naturally retries the same cutoff-based query (sweep.ts sweepOnce, the per-entry registry loop).
retention-gc-worker.poisonMessageHandling: There is no per-row poison-message concept (bulk cutoff-based DELETE, not a per-item queue); a systematically failing entry (e.g. a bad identifier) is caught per-tick, logged with {table, code}, and left for the next tick -- the boot-time validateRegistry() call fails closed (throws) before the loop starts if any registry entry has an invalid identifier or missing globalDelete flag, so malformed entries never reach runtime processing (index.ts validateRegistry, called from createWorker).

tenantScoped.reason: Both runCadence transactions (claimAttempt and the publish transaction in runCadenceInner) set the AUDIT_ANCHOR_PUBLISH bypass grant with app.tenant_id=SYSTEM_TENANT_ID (setBypassGucs) to read every auditChainEnabled tenant's anchor row in one cadence run, but the manifest it builds and the lastPublishedAt / publishPausedUntil updates it writes are always partitioned per tenantId (AnchorRow[] per tenant; updateMany scoped to tenantsInManifest in runCadenceInner and persistPause) -- a system-wide read, never a cross-tenant data write.

audit-anchor-publisher.idempotent: One publish per cadence boundary, decided by a marker under a lock. Every run sets SET LOCAL lock_timeout (setLockTimeout, DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 s) and then takes the BLOCKING pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('audit-anchor-publish')) (advisoryXactLock, ADVISORY_LOCK_KEY); a wait past the timeout raises SQLSTATE 55P03, read through pgErrorCode (isLockNotAvailable) and returned as lock_held, which is not a failure. Under the lock, isBoundaryPublished reads the system_settings marker audit_anchor_last_published_boundary -- on an install that predates the marker, MAX(audit_chain_anchors.last_published_at) >= boundary stands in -- and an equal boundary returns skipped_already_published. The check runs in claimAttempt and again inside the publish transaction, which writes the marker (Prisma upsert) in the same commit as the manifest pointer (audit_anchor_previous_manifest). The boundary is the one createAnchorScheduler armed the timer for, not the clock at publish time, so it alone fixes the marker, the artifact key (buildManifestArtifactKey) and anchoredAt. ensureDeploymentIdMatch is NOT a single-owner lock: it pins DEPLOYMENT_ID in system_settings (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) so a publisher configured for another deployment refuses to boot (DeploymentIdMismatchError); a second instance with the same DEPLOYMENT_ID boots and is serialized by the lock and the marker. On ECS the service runs at most one task (desired_count = min(1, worker_desired_count), deployment_maximum_percent = 100, deployment_minimum_healthy_percent = 0), so a deploy stops the old task before starting the new one.
audit-anchor-publisher.retryPolicy: Two layers. In process: createAnchorScheduler awaits one run for the current boundary at boot, then re-arms a setTimeout computed from the wall clock after every run (no setInterval). A failed run at any stage (isRetryable) is retried for the SAME boundary every ANCHOR_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS (15 min), at most ANCHOR_MAX_RETRIES_PER_BOUNDARY (3) times per process and only while the retry falls at least ANCHOR_RETRY_STOP_BEFORE_NEXT_MS (30 min) before the next boundary; past the 3 it logs audit-anchor-publisher.retries_exhausted and waits. That in-process bound is the only one on a failure before claimAttempt writes the count (the tenants read failing, the database unreachable), which the persisted cap never sees. lock_held and upload_cap_reached are not retried; they wait for the next boundary or the next boot run. Persisted cap: claimAttempt counts every run that passes the marker and tenant checks in system_settings.audit_anchor_upload_attempts ({boundary, count}; findUnique + Prisma upsert under the advisory lock) in its OWN transaction, committed before the publish transaction opens, so neither a rollback nor a crash after the PUT resets it and a crash-looping task cannot keep uploading; a run with no chain-enabled tenant returns skipped_no_tenants without counting. A run whose count exceeds AUDIT_ANCHOR_UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_CAP (3) uploads nothing and returns upload_cap_reached. A stored count that does not parse (JSON or schema; parseUploadAttempts) is overwritten in the same claim transaction with {boundary: this boundary, count: AUDIT_ANCHOR_UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_CAP + 1}, so the run reports upload_cap_reached (fail-closed for that boundary) and the next boundary counts 1 again. A commit lost after a successful upload rolls the publish transaction back and writes no pause (commit_failed_after_upload); the retry re-PUTs the same key and bucket versioning keeps the earlier version. Bounds: lock wait 10 s; the upload to every destination 60 s as a whole (DEFAULT_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, an AbortController plus untilAborted); each transaction 90 s (DEFAULT_TX_TIMEOUT_MS). ECS stopTimeout is 120 s, and SIGTERM stops the scheduler arming and waits for the in-flight run (AnchorScheduler.stop) before the pool is closed.
audit-anchor-publisher.poisonMessageHandling: There is no per-item queue to poison; the unit is a cadence boundary. Each failed run (fail) logs audit-anchor-publisher.cadence_failed and writes one AUDIT_ANCHOR_PUBLISH_FAILED row through emitAudit, which never throws and sends a failed outbox write to the dead-letter logger -- per boundary, at most 3 counted runs across restarts (one row each) plus the one cap row; a failure before the count is written is uncounted and bounded instead by the scheduler, at most 1 + ANCHOR_MAX_RETRIES_PER_BOUNDARY runs per boundary per process start. An upload failure also persists publish_paused_until on the manifest's tenants until the next boundary (persistPause, its own transaction after the rollback); that pause is held by the audit-outbox worker, which stops advancing those tenants' chains, and no longer holds publishing -- every chain-enabled tenant is published, and a successful publish clears it. The first run past the cap logs audit-anchor-publisher.upload_cap_reached (alarmed) and writes one UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_CAP_REACHED failure row for the boundary (UPLOAD_ATTEMPT_COUNT_UNREADABLE, with countUnreadable: true on the log line, when the stored count did not parse); later runs for that boundary log only. A boundary that is never committed is reported by the next publish as MISSING_PRIOR_CADENCE_PUBLICATION (audit-anchor-publisher.missing_prior_cadence).

audit-chain-verify-worker.$modules-note: DB logic is inlined in the script itself (no src/workers counterpart) -- mechanical greps (rawSql/destructive/emitsAudit/usesSecurityDefiner) run against this file directly, per plan review S1.

tenantScoped.reason: runTick enumerates ALL tenants under the named SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE_TENANT_LOOKUP bypass grant (tenants carries the same RLS policy as every other table since migration 20261022000000_tenants_rls) and calls verifyTenantChain once per tenantId, and the underlying query filters WHERE tenant_id = $1 (audit-chain-verify-worker.ts runTick, verifyTenantChain) -- a system-wide read loop, but each verification pass is scoped to a single tenant's chain: via its own withTenantRls context, or for the __system__ sentinel (which withTenantRls refuses) under the AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_SENTINEL_READ bypass grant, with the returned rows asserted to belong to it.

audit-chain-verify-worker.idempotent: Verification is read-only (SELECT ... ORDER BY chain_seq ASC, no writes) and re-walks the same rows deterministically every tick, so re-running never mutates state and always reproduces the same ok/firstTamperedSeq result for an unchanged chain (audit-chain-verify-worker.ts:68-121).
audit-chain-verify-worker.retryPolicy: No retry semantics: a per-tenant verify failure is caught, logged ("tenant=%s verify threw"), and the loop continues to the next tenant; the NEXT hourly tick (fixed TICK_INTERVAL_MS, no backoff) re-attempts the same tenant from scratch (audit-chain-verify-worker.ts:130-173,208-215).
audit-chain-verify-worker.poisonMessageHandling: Not applicable -- there is no queue or per-row claim, only a full per-tenant re-scan every tick; a tamper finding is reported via CHAIN_VERIFY_FAILED console logging with hysteresis (re-alert only on clean-to-failed transition or every 24h while failed, audit-chain-verify-worker.ts:145-163) rather than any dead-letter mechanism.
